findings.title: Buffer Overflow in Queue Operations
findings.untrusted_source: The data element size and buffer length provided during queue initialization.
findings.trigger: If the buffer length or element size is manipulated to be incorrect, memcpy can write out of bounds.
findings.assumptions: The buffer size and element size are not validated to ensure they fit within the allocated memory.

findings.title: Resource Leaks in Queue Initialization
findings.untrusted_source: Initialization of mutex and condition variable.
findings.trigger: If initialization fails, resources may not be properly cleaned up.
findings.assumptions: There is no error handling for mutex and condition variable initialization failures.

findings.title: Use After Free in Queue Operations
findings.untrusted_source: The queue buffer provided during initialization.
findings.trigger: If the queue buffer is freed after initialization but before use, memcpy can operate on invalid memory.
findings.assumptions: The queue buffer is not checked for validity before each operation.

findings.title: Race Condition in Queue Operations
findings.untrusted_source: Concurrent access to the queue by multiple threads.
findings.trigger: If multiple threads attempt to push or pop elements concurrently, race conditions can lead to incorrect queue state.
findings.assumptions: The mutex is not correctly used to protect all critical sections.
